title: Power Apps: row summaries in model-driven apps reach GCC and GCC High
summary: Hold: the cost and licensing fields account for user licences but omit the documented consumption model for AI Builder prompts. The roadmap details and both configuration paths are supported, and the briefing appropriately reports the conflicting default-state guidance.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists November CY2026 as the release target.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

    "GCC",

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.

claims.claim: Admins and makers enable and configure row summaries for model-driven app users.
claims.quote: Admins and makers enable and configure row summaries for users in their model-driven apps.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Row summaries read record data and generate a natural-language overview.
claims.quote: The feature reads the data on the current record and generates a short, natural-language summary that highlights key information

claims.claim: Summaries appear in the Insights bar on main forms.
claims.quote: From the Insights bar at the top of main forms.

claims.claim: Users access summaries on view pages through the Summary action.
claims.quote: From view pages by selecting the inline Summary action in the grid, which opens the summary for a record in a modal popup.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Makers configure a table's summary prompt to specify which columns to include.
claims.quote: Write a custom prompt to specify which columns should be included in a Copilot-generated row summary.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Power Platform Copilot FAQ says Copilot adheres to existing data permissions and policies.
claims.quote: Copilot adheres to existing data permissions and policies

claims.claim: The Power Platform Copilot FAQ says responses are based only on data the user personally can access.
claims.quote: its responses to you're based only on data that you personally can access.

claims.claim: Learn documents a column-security limitation for form fill assistance.
claims.quote: Fields that have column security aren't currently supported.

claims.claim: That form-fill column-security limitation is not documented as a row-summary limitation.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps row summary usage analytics report column security secured columns. Opened record-summaries, configure-form-row-summary, faq-record-summaries and form-filling-assistance; no row-summary-specific column-security limitation stated.

claims.claim: AI-generated summaries can be wrong.
claims.quote: The response generated might be incorrect or misleading and could cause unintended outcomes from the flow or app.

claims.claim: The licensing model is per-user rather than mixed user licensing and consumption.
claims.quote: In Power Apps and Power Automate, AI Builder features consume either AI Builder credits (Licensing and AI Builder credits), or Copilot Credits (Licensing and Copilot Credits).
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to mixed. Retain the documented user-licence requirements and append: 'Row summaries rely on AI Builder to execute summary prompts; AI Builder features in Power Apps consume AI Builder credits or Copilot Credits.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/common/faq-record-summaries and https://learn.microsoft.com/ai-builder/administer-licensing.

Under Power Apps, locate Row summaries in the Summary section.
Select the environment, and then select Edit setting.

claims.claim: Show row summary does not hide Microsoft-provided summaries or summaries configured through another application or experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a separate tenant switch specific to GCC and GCC High for row summaries.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps row summaries GCC GCC High government pricing licensing default enable tenant setting; "row summaries" "GCC" "setting". Read record-summaries, copilot-hub and powerapps-us-government; no separate cloud-specific tenant control found.

claims.claim: The documented row-summary availability control is an environment setting rather than a cloud-specific switch.
claims.quote: Use the Copilot settings experience in the Power Platform admin center as the primary environment-level control for row summaries

claims.claim: The environment setting is the primary environment-level row-summary availability control.
claims.quote: Use the Copilot settings experience in the Power Platform admin center as the primary environment-level control for row summaries

claims.claim: A preview Copilot control allows specific users or all users except an exclusion list.
claims.quote: Admins can define who within an environment can use Copilot capabilities in model-driven apps—either by explicitly allowing specific users or allowing all users except a defined exclusion list. This capability is currently in preview

claims.claim: The preview user allow/exclude control is only for environments activated for Managed Environments.
claims.quote: This capability is currently in preview and is only for environments activated for managed environments, with a subset of Copilot features adhering to it.

claims.claim: Power Apps Row summary is listed as adhering to the preview user allow/exclude configuration.
claims.quote: | Power Apps | Row summary |

claims.claim: The Copilot hub page does not state whether the preview user allow/exclude control is available in GCC or GCC High.
claims.quote: Searched: "row summaries" "GCC" "setting"; Power Apps row summaries GCC GCC High government pricing licensing default enable tenant setting. Opened copilot-hub in full and powerapps-us-government; the hub gives no GCC/GCC High availability statement for this control.

claims.claim: The older AI insight cards location currently exposes the same row-summary control.
claims.quote: The same control is currently also available as AI insight cards in the environment feature settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the AI insight cards settings location will be removed in a future release.
claims.quote: The AI insight cards location will be removed in a future release.

claims.claim: A row-summary-specific usage report is not documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps row summary usage analytics report column security secured columns; "row summaries" "usage" "report". Opened copilot-hub and record-summaries; hub Power Apps analytics covers data entry and data exploration agents, not a row-summary-specific report.

claims.claim: Row-summary generation sends record data to a generative AI service.
claims.quote: The feature reads the data on the current record and generates a short, natural-language summary that highlights key information

claims.claim: The underlying summary prompts execute through Microsoft's hosted generative AI services.
claims.quote: Prompt builder prompts run on Azure OpenAI Service hosted by Microsoft.

claims.claim: The change's known cost is low, consisting of review and communication rather than metered consumption.
claims.quote: AI Builder is licensed on a capacity basis. Building custom and testing models (including prompts) doesn't require AI Builder credits or Copilot Credits. Running them in agents, agent flows, apps, or flows consume these credits.
claims.fix: Set cost to variable and replace the cost rationale with: 'Variable. Row summaries rely on AI Builder to execute prompts; AI Builder features in Power Apps consume AI Builder credits or Copilot Credits.' Add the same consumption statement to Cost and licensing, citing https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/common/faq-record-summaries and https://learn.microsoft.com/ai-builder/administer-licensing. Retain the narrower government-specific pricing gap; do not infer a government-specific token rate.

claims.claim: Government licensing terms may differ from the general product guidance.
